item.title: Global consumption-based deforestation carbon emissions and regional hotspots: 2001–2020
item.description:
Global consumption-based deforestation carbon emissions and regional hotspots: 2001–2020
Dongmei Tang, Yuanzhi Yao, Rui Li, and Xia Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8345–8359, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8345-2026, 2026
We present a global, gridded dataset (1 km resolution) of consumption-based deforestation carbon emissions for the period 2001 to 2020. Our dataset shows that deforestation emissions embodied in international trade account for 31.8 % of global deforestation emissions. It provides spatially explicit information to support analyses of consumption-driven deforestation emissions and inform climate mitigation and policy assessments.

item.title: ALPAKAS: Alpine hydrographs and catchment attributes for karst springs
item.description:
ALPAKAS: Alpine hydrographs and catchment attributes for karst springs
Felix Joger, Pauline Thinius, Zhao Chen, Andreas Hartmann, Nico Goldscheider, Tanja Liesch, Gerhard Schubert, and Stefan Broda
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8377–8406, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8377-2026, 2026
Karst aquifers are important water sources in the Alps, but comparable spring discharge data have been lacking. We created ALPAKAS, the first large-sample benchmark dataset dedicated to karst springs across the wider Alpine region. It provides 242 daily and 182 hourly harmonized and quality-controlled discharge records, along with catchment delineations, meteorological time series, catchment attributes, and karst-specific indices. The dataset supports comparative analyses and model benchmarking.

item.title: Long-term observations of hydrography, phytoplankton pigments, and suspended particles in Potter Cove (Antarctica), 1991–2025
item.description:
Long-term observations of hydrography, phytoplankton pigments, and suspended particles in Potter Cove (Antarctica), 1991–2025
Irene Ruth Schloss, Luz Marina Suklje, María Liliana Quartino, Gustavo Adolfo Ferreyra, Oscar González, Alejandro Ulrich, Silvia A. Rodríguez, Eduardo Ruiz Barlett, Gabriela Tosonotto, Facundo Matías Barrera, Gabriela Campana, Dolores Deregibus, Camila Neder, Kerstin Jerosch, and Mohamed Adjou
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-846,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Antarctica is changing, but long-term coastal observations remain rare. This study brings together more than 30 years of data from Potter Cove, Antarctica, including seawater temperature, salt content, microscopic plant pigments, and suspended particles. By combining thousands of observations collected across seasons, this dataset provides a unique resource for understanding environmental change and ecosystem responses, aiding to understand how Antarctic coastal waters may change in the future.

item.title: A ground-based multi-instrument remote sensing dataset of in-cloud vertical air motion, particle terminal fall velocity, and hydrometeor classification over Xi'an, China (2021–2022)
item.description:
A ground-based multi-instrument remote sensing dataset of in-cloud vertical air motion, particle terminal fall velocity, and hydrometeor classification over Xi'an, China (2021–2022)
Huige Di, Yun Yuan, Shuling Hu, Ning Chen, Yufeng Wang, Qing Yan, and Dengxin Hua
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-901,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Clouds influence rainfall, but continuous observations of air motion and falling particles inside clouds are difficult. We used ground-based radar and temperature measurements from Xi’an, China, during 2021–2022 to create a dataset covering 541 observation days. It records air motion, falling particles, and seven types of cloud and precipitation particles every 5 seconds at 30-meter vertical intervals. The dataset supports research on cloud structure and precipitation formation.

item.title: Ecological change in the native Scottish pinewoods since 1971 – data from the Bunce 2018–2022 re-survey
item.description:
Ecological change in the native Scottish pinewoods since 1971 – data from the Bunce 2018–2022 re-survey
Claire M. Wood, Simon M. Smart, Fiona M. Seaton, Andy McMullen, Susan E. Ward, Karen Hornigold, Chris Nichols, and Clare McW. H. Benskin
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8361–8376, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8361-2026, 2026
Between 2018 and 2022, an ecological survey of the native pinewoods of Scotland was carried out; a repeat survey of the same sites completed in 1971. Data collected from this unique and biodiverse habitat includes information on ground flora, soils, forest structure and general site information from 27 major pinewood sites. Questions addressing the threats and changes occurring in the pinewood habitat can now be explored across a 50 year time span for the first time.

item.title: Global gridded air-sea oxygen flux inferred from a machine learning-based dissolved oxygen product
item.description:
Global gridded air-sea oxygen flux inferred from a machine learning-based dissolved oxygen product
Yuming Jin, Britton B. Stephens, Eric J. Morgan, Manfredi Manizza, and Jonathan Sharp
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8407–8439, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8407-2026, 2026
We produce monthly air-sea O2 flux estimates (2004-2024) on a 1°×1° grid using machine learning-based dissolved oxygen fields (GOBAI-O2, Sharp et al., 2023). Fluxes are calculated with multiple gas exchange schemes and wind products, then constrained to match independent regional to global annual mean flux estimates. We evaluate flux seasonal cycles and annual patterns against atmospheric O2 observations and quantify flux uncertainties from multiple sources.
